questions.q: Why did Billy get angry when the troop-horse mentioned his "family on his father's side"?
choices: His father had been sold away when he was young
Every mule hates to be reminded his father was a donkey
His father had run away from a battle long ago
He thought the horse was making fun of his name
questions.evidence: every mule hates to be reminded that his father was a donkey

questions.q: Billy and the troop-horse reared up to fight. What stopped them?
choices: The narrator shouted at them from the gun
Their drivers came running with lanterns
Two Tails called out to them to be quiet
The bullocks pushed in between them
questions.evidence: Children, what are you fighting about there? Be quiet.

questions.q: Why did Billy and the troop-horse suddenly become friendly again after their quarrel?
choices: The narrator gave them both biscuits
They both disliked Two Tails the elephant
They realized they served in the same battery
They were both too tired to keep on fighting

questions.q: Two Tails' captain called him a "Pachydermatous Anachronism." What does Two Tails say this means?
choices: Betwixt and between
Bravest of all the beasts
Too old to work any longer
Stronger than any gun in camp

questions.q: According to Two Tails, why is he afraid when the guns fire?
choices: The loud noise hurts his very large ears
He was once badly wounded by a bursting shell
He can picture in his head what a shell will do
The smoke makes it hard for him to breathe
questions.evidence: I can see inside my head what will happen when a shell bursts

questions.q: What is one difference between Two Tails and the troop-horse?
choices: Only the horse trusts the man who drives him
The horse is afraid of dogs, but Two Tails is not
The horse pulls guns, but Two Tails carries soldiers
The horse has fought in wars, but Two Tails never has

questions.q: Two Tails says, "I know just enough to be uncomfortable, and not enough to go on in spite of it." What does he mean?
choices: He has forgotten most of what his driver taught him at the camp
He sees danger well enough to fear it, but can't overcome it
He is too clever to obey any order that he does not like
He needs more training before he can pull the big guns
questions.evidence: I know just enough to be uncomfortable, and not enough to go on in spite of it.

questions.q: To make the others understand fear, what did Two Tails do?
choices: He told them a story about a tiger hunt
He stamped until the guns rattled
He trumpeted furiously at the top of his trumpet
He pulled up his picket and walked toward them
questions.evidence: He began trumpeting furiously at the top of his trumpet.

questions.q: What is the one thing an elephant fears more than anything else, according to the narrator?
choices: A small dog barking at his feet
A camel that runs loose at night
The sound of a bugle in the dark
A mouse running under his feet
questions.evidence: it is a little barking dog

questions.q: The narrator never let Vixen know he understood beast talk, "or she would have taken all sorts of liberties." What does this mean?
choices: She would have run away to live with the soldiers
She would have behaved too boldly and done as she pleased
She would have told all his secrets to the other animals in camp
She would have refused to eat anything but biscuits
questions.evidence: she would have taken all sorts of liberties

questions.q: When the young mule asked why they have to fight at all, what did the animals answer?
choices: To protect the people of the camp
To earn good food and warm stables
Because they are told to; it is an order
Because fighting is what they were born for

questions.q: What did the gun-bullocks proudly say about themselves before leaving?
choices: They were the strongest beasts in all the army
They were the only ones that night who had not been afraid
They had pulled more big guns than any other yoke in the battery
They were the cleverest animals in the whole camp
questions.evidence: we are the only people to-night who have not been afraid

questions.q: Why did the bullocks panic and run when they learned Vixen's master was a white man?
choices: He had beaten them once on the parade-ground
Englishmen eat beef, and the cattle dislike it
He was the officer who had them yoked to the gun
They thought he had come to take their grazing

questions.q: "Billy the Mule stumped off with the swaggering limp of an old campaigner." What does "swaggering" tell you about how he walked?
choices: Slowly and sadly, as if hurt
Proudly and boldly, chest out
Quietly, trying not to be seen
Nervously, looking all around
questions.evidence: the swaggering limp of an old campaigner

questions.q: What was the troop-horse doing as the Lancers rode past in the grand parade?
choices: Leading the Viceroy's own carriage
Setting the time for all his squadron
Pulling a cart full of the band's drums
Carrying the flag at the very front
questions.evidence: setting the time for all his squadron

questions.q: How did the Amir of Afghanistan feel as the long line of troops came straight toward him?
choices: Bored, since he had seen many parades
Pleased, and he waved to the soldiers
Alarmed, as if he might need to escape
Angry that the rain had spoiled the day
questions.evidence: his eyes began to get bigger and bigger

questions.q: The Central Asian chief says, "Would it were so in Afghanistan!" What does he mean?
choices: He wishes Afghanistan had as many elephants
He wishes his people obeyed orders like this
He wishes it rained less in his own country
He wishes his own army had such fine big guns
questions.evidence: for there we obey only our own wills

questions.q: What is the main lesson of this part of the story?
choices: The bravest animal is always the strongest one
Each animal should fight in exactly the same way
An army works because everyone obeys the one above
Animals are always wiser than the men who drive them
questions.evidence: An order was given, and they obeyed.
